what: The Rose provides breast screening and diagnostic care through Houston-area centers and mobile units.
Its patient navigators help uninsured patients arrange cancer treatment and practical support.
Sponsored care, translation, transport and childcare assistance seek to reduce barriers from diagnosis through recovery.
strengths: Original return distinguishes unduplicated uninsured people and insured versus uninsured treatment navigations.
Primary controlled navigation evidence gives both positive and null alternative-provider regimes.
Current BCCS, transport and childcare mechanisms connect care access to signed household resources.
reservations: The conditional price combines full annual recipient cost with only a limited modeled uninsured channel.
Small positive health-plus-income denominator is sensitive to unmeasured utility, burden and partner cost.
Navigation counts and faster resolution are not proven stage-shift, survival or QALY gains.

sections.what: The Rose provides breast screening and diagnostic care through Houston-area centers and mobile units. Its patient navigators help uninsured patients arrange cancer treatment and practical support. Sponsored care, translation, transport and childcare assistance seek to reduce barriers from diagnosis through recovery.
sections.monitoring: Original FY 2025 return reports 8,571 individual unduplicated uninsured women and 187 patients navigated into treatment:177 uninsured and 10 insured. The visually checked FY 2025 annual report page 22 instead lists 178 uninsured cancers and 588 support patients, versus original return 177 uninsured cancers and 812 support; definitions differ and are not combined. Neither source establishes completed appropriate treatment, unique households or causal stage improvement. Repeated interactions, screening exams, biopsies and insured/mobile services are not added as disjoint beneficiaries. Mobile residence spans 62 counties; .8 Houstonshare is a retained judgment, not measured MSA residence. Request unique local household histories, usual-provider access, time-to-treatment, completed treatment, stage-specific clinical outcomes, false-positive/overdiagnosis effects, and net patient/caregiver cash/time burdens.
sections.qualitative: Original DenverRCT randomized 993 abnormal screens (628 breast) and found diagnostic-resolution effects varied by abnormality, with no significant breastBIRADS 4/5 improvement. Original LosAngelesRCT 1,708 women found no six-month overall resolution improvement (55% versus 56%). Original multisite PNRP showed no first 90 daybenefit and later 91–365 day improvements in resolution/treatment initiation, especially where usual care delayed; it does not measure local survival, utility orQALYs. These support positive and strong-alternative/null regimes, not empirical .25/.3 multipliers. Original 2024 CISNET screening decision analysis includes false positives, benign biopsies and overdiagnosis alongside lifetime screening benefits; serial screening against no screening cannot calibrate one annual local navigation cohort. No diagnosis count, apparent survival from earlier detection or time-to-treatment hazard ratio is directly converted into lives saved. The finite .2 utility/two-year trajectory remains judgment and its null/weak/strong sensitivities are visible.
sections.cost: Initial $42.02 M per better life (health 4.008925 plus signed income−.204127) is preserved exactly. Full exposure burdens alone, keeping 187 clinical subgroup, give $178.84 M. Mapping to observed 177 uninsured navigations gives current $238.29 M: health 3.300950 plus signed income−2.630090 =.670860 healthy-year equivalents. This is not evidence the whole portfolio became 5.7 times worse; it corrects exposure accounting and a subgroup boundary in a deliberately partial conditional reference. Full cost $15,986,247 includes insured imaging and other activities whose benefits are not estimated here. All-program recognized-cost sensitivity is $13,174,486 but remains broader than the modeled channel. A judged uninsured-patient-share allocation ($13,174,486*8,571/41,186) yields $40.87 M; this is not observed navigation cost, full resource cost or an eligible marginal offer. .95 individual-to-consumption mapping and .8 local share are judgments. Full exposure 8,142.45 proxies each retain $20 incremental access/time cost and .0001 one-off harm independent of b; judged changed union 2,035.6125, resource-success 203.56125, clinical trajectory 12.61125 are subsets not added cohorts. Only positive medical/work/practical aid receives .5 overlap reduction; negative amounts remain full and all recipient household amounts enter one log at $20,000 baseline. Net practical support$300 excludes displaced charity/family aid, benefit withdrawals and taxes; medical and caregiver earnings zero are unknown-neutral, not measured zero. No retail charity bill, gross salary or full lifetime survivor wages are income. External BCCS/partner treatment resources and aid transfers have distinct payer/provider incidence, localized once; $5,000 per incremental clinical trajectory stress is explicit judgment, not measured cost. Clinical-null, financial-only, failed-benefit b 0 with full negatives, actual no-exposure, adverse, weak-alternative, low/high burdens and payer loss cases remain separate. Whole portfolio EV and donor-funded additional capacity remain unknown.
sections.funding: FY 2025 original expense $15,866,042 plus $120,205 netted event cost gives $15,986,247. FY 2024 $16,471,873 plus $96,459 gives $16,568,332. FY 2023 $15,265,960 plus $81,601 gives $15,347,561. Expense-side Schedule D removed expenses are zero in these returns; no populated rental-expense addback recovered. Partner treatment and unrecognized volunteers remain unknown. Paid clinical revenue, BCCS and CPRIT grants are baseline funding, not proof of gift-driven expansion. Original return all-program expense $13,174,486 includes insured and uninsured medical work; no observed uninsured navigation budget allocation is established. Public and partner treatment opportunity costs are outside the recipient budget and central zero is unknown-neutral. Insured program revenue subsidizes care but does not prove donation responsiveness.

model.costScope: Full annual recipient expense against limited uninsured navigation/access hypothesis; all insured screening, other medical and education benefits unknown, not zero. Not whole portfolio EV or marginal gift.
model.geographicAttribution: Original uninsured women and navigation counts span recipient Southeast Texas services; mobile residence62counties. Houston .8 share is retained judgment, not observed MSA residence; .5 sensitivity.
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=N*unique*b. Clinical=clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*discounted finite years minus all exposed harms; geography once. Resources are joint household logs, positive-only overlap, full exposed costs; distinct payer treatment/transfer costs localized once. Headline=10*C/(health+signed resource equivalents).
model.counterfactual: Existing insurance, BCCS, Harris Health, other screening/navigation providers and family support retained
model.attribution: The .25 additional response and .3 clinical-benefit response are explicit hypotheses against public/partner alternatives; original trials support variable navigation mechanisms, not local coefficients. No HR-to-QALY or diagnosis-to-survival shortcut.
model.uncertainty: Current cohort mapping improved from original return; utility, response, resources, public treatment opportunity costs, localshare and gift capacity remain unmeasured. Small positive conditional denominator is sensitive and not empirical portfolio EV.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional timely appropriate treatment/access, after false-positive and overdiagnosis harms; current187 nav includes177uninsured and10insured in original return, not187new uninsured lives saved.
